diagnostics.name: Backend verifier

items.text: Manouchehr Motaki said that if the US does not implement the agreement, Iran should not give Trump an advantage. He emphasized that it is time for action and that the US has rejected negotiations with the Islamic Republic. He also mentioned that if Trump loses the US midterm elections, there will be two years of confusion, but if he wins, Israel will push them towards war.

The Director General of Urban Environmental Improvement of Mashhad Municipality announced a ban on dog walking in the city's parks. This directive has been communicated to the 13 municipal districts. Over 200 informational signs about this ban have been installed in Mashhad's parks.

Michel Aoun, the US ambassador to Lebanon, said Hezbollah receives its orders only from the Islamic Republic. He added that Lebanese people agree on disarming Hezbollah. He also emphasized that Hezbollah takes no action against Israeli attacks.

Mohsen Namjoo announced that after about 20 years, he is on the way back to Iran. He said it does not matter to him whether he has musical or cultural activities in Iran and he wants to be with his family and friends. He also planned to hold concerts in Toronto, Washington DC, and New York.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated at the farewell ceremony of new ambassadors that the Islamic Republic's approach in international relations is peaceful and interaction-oriented. He emphasized that countries' interests should be met through interaction without greed. The new ambassadors must accurately explain this approach to the people of the world.

Leila Abolhasani, detained during the January 2026 protests, has been sentenced to death on charges of moharebeh. Her case is currently under review by the Supreme Court following an appeal. She has been held in Dolatabad Prison in Isfahan since January 8, 2026.

Kaveh Madani, an Iranian water researcher, received the 2026 Stockholm Water Prize from the King of Sweden. The award was given in recognition of his research and activities in water resource management and governance. The prize includes one million Swedish kronor and a crystal trophy.

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, criticized the Islamic Republic's financial policies in a post on X, calling for the country's financial resources to be allocated to the Iranian people. He said that instead of injecting billions of dollars into its terrorist proxy groups, the Iranian government should spend this money on its own people. These remarks come amid intensified US financial sanctions against Iran.

Asieh Ramazani, a 39-year-old woman and mother of two, was killed by direct gunfire from the Islamic Republic forces during the suppression of the December 1404 protests in Tehran. Her family criticized the handling of her body and the failure to return her personal belongings. They emphasize that the full circumstances of her death remain unclear.

Ahmad Zeraatkar stated that 40% of the damaged capacity of South Pars has returned to production. Deputy Paknejad said the debris removal of South Pars has been completed. Reconstruction is being carried out in an organized and planned manner.

The Pentagon has prepared a plan to review the US military presence in Europe. This plan is set to be presented to the US Secretary of Defense next month. Some European officials are concerned about a possible reduction of the US military presence in Europe.

A citizen criticized the high cost of medicine in a video sent to Iran International. He said the treatment cost for a simple cold is nearly three million tomans. This issue highlights patients' concerns.

Ebrahim Azizi, head of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, stated that any dialogue must be conducted from a position of strength and with acceptance of the realities on the ground. He emphasized that the confrontation with the enemy is not only military but also includes economic, cultural, social, media, diplomatic, and psychological arenas.

Mediators from Qatar, Oman, and Pakistan are trying to restore the Strait of Hormuz to normal conditions and start negotiations with the US. However, there is a significant gap between the Islamic Republic's demands and Washington's position. Continued economic pressure could reduce the Islamic Republic's ability to meet essential needs.

Caroline Lewitt, White House spokesperson, stated that currently there are no negotiations between the United States and the Islamic Republic. She emphasized that all options regarding the Islamic Republic remain on Donald Trump's table. These remarks were made in an interview with Fox News.

The mayor of Sanandaj announced that about 55% of the city's urban fabric is in inefficient or worn-out areas. Informal settlements and ownership issues have challenged safe urban development. Additionally, the average age of the municipality's construction machinery has reached 38 to 40 years.

Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, Qatar's Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, met with Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf in Tehran. They discussed regional developments and efforts to reduce tensions. The Qatari Foreign Minister stated that dialogue is the best way to resolve disputes.

Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, Qatar's Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, met with Masoud Pezeshkian, head of the Iranian government, in Tehran. He also met with Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Speaker of the Iranian Parliament, to discuss solutions for resuming negotiations between Washington and Tehran.

Mojtaba Khamenei has been introduced as the third leader of the Islamic Republic but has not appeared in public or been heard. This absence may indicate the government's weakness or delay the political death of the Islamic Republic. Previously, the regime displayed its leaders everywhere, but now it releases messages from the new leader without showing him.

Hamidreza Amiri denied the accusations made by his wife Vida Rabani regarding domestic violence and property seizure. He stated that his wife's account is fundamentally incorrect and does not match the facts and documents. Amiri asked the audience to review the narratives and evidence from both sides.

Majid Bahiraei, a political prisoner and detainee from the December 1404 protests, is serving his sentence in Malayer prison. He was sentenced to two years and two months of imprisonment by Branch 101 of the Nahavand Revolutionary Court. This information was confirmed by a source close to his family.

Hojatollah Nikimaleki has been appointed as the chairman of Digikala's board. He previously managed the media of the Execution of Imam Khomeini's Order and the Afseran social network. This news was published by Iran International.

Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, the Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Qatar, met with Masoud Pezeshkian during his visit to Tehran. He also discussed the resumption of negotiations between Washington and Tehran with Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf. The Qatari foreign minister emphasized that dialogue is the best way to resolve disputes and prevent further escalation of tensions.

Le Monde reported that Persian Gulf countries, after six months of intense tension between Tehran and Washington, are trying to reduce their dependence on the Strait of Hormuz for oil exports by building and developing pipelines. The UAE is expanding its Habshan to Fujairah pipeline to reach a capacity of about 3.6 million barrels per day.
The World Humanoid Robot Competition in Beijing ended after five days of contests. Robots set new records in sports and practical skills. Their unexpected movements amazed the spectators.
Elham Khalas, a Bahá'í citizen residing in Isfahan, was arrested after appearing at the General and Revolutionary Prosecutor's Office of the city. She was transferred to Dolatabad Prison in Isfahan.

The Intelligence Organization of the IRGC stated that the Islamic Republic has moved beyond mere survival and is now stabilizing its resilience. It is not only responding to attacks but increasing its strategic initiative. Military readiness to deliver a decisive blow to the enemy is one of its key activities.

Citizens report a sharp increase in the prices of baby formula, medical costs, and school tuition. Snapp drivers complain about technical issues and reduced income. Additionally, internet outages have caused programmers to lose their jobs.

Mohsen Rezaei warned the US that if it initiates hostility against the Islamic Republic, it will face severe consequences for its military and economic interests. He emphasized that the US must first fulfill the Islamic Republic's conditions before Tehran reopens the Strait of Hormuz. Rezaei also stated that they do not trust the US, which has repeatedly betrayed diplomacy.

Israel Hayom newspaper wrote that Israel must remain prepared for the scenario of renewed direct conflict with the Islamic Republic. The newspaper emphasized that economic pressures and sanctions, while limiting Tehran's financial resources, are not sufficient alone to change the Islamic Republic's policies. The report was by Babak Es-haqi from Iran International.

Reports indicate fuel shortages and long queues at gas stations. At the same time, the atmosphere in some Iranian cities has become highly securitized. This information comes from public reports received by Iran International.

David Barnea, former Mossad chief, said Donald Trump understands that the Iranian regime should not be allowed to remain in power. He described the severe sanctions against the Islamic Republic as a correct but only one step. Barnea called for intensifying economic, diplomatic, and operational measures against the Iranian regime until its fall.

On the morning of Wednesday, 5 Shahrivar, part of a glacier in the Himalayas collapsed, causing a deadly flood. The incident resulted in at least 165 deaths and over a thousand missing people. Scientists are still investigating the exact cause of this disaster.
In a village in Sabzevar, Khorasan Razavi, citizens have written protest slogans and support for the Pahlavi family on the walls. This was reported through videos sent to Iran International.

Associated Press reported that about 65% of the US Patriot interceptor missiles have been used in the war with the Islamic Republic. This equals approximately 1,500 out of a total of 2,330 missiles. The US interceptor missile stocks in Europe have reached a critical level.

Donald Trump stated that Russia has behaved very well regarding the Strait of Hormuz. He also said Vladimir Putin will not attack NATO territory. Trump signed an executive order to rename Lake Ontario to 'Lake America'.

In recent years, the criminal responsibility of business owners for customers' behavior has increased. This issue is used as a tool for social control, and even without direct involvement, the business owner may be punished. This approach challenges criminal law principles because criminal responsibility should be personal, and ownership or management alone does not create liability.
Donald Trump said that they moved 24 vessels through the Strait of Hormuz last night and do this regularly. He added that this does not mean the military mission is over.

The family of Lindsay and Craig Foreman has asked the British government to arrange consular visits and check their health status. Despite the return of British embassy staff to Tehran, no consular meeting has taken place yet. Joe Bennet was able to speak with his mother by phone for the first time in three months.

A US source stated that any agreement between the Islamic Republic and Oman is not important to Washington. It was also said that the Strait of Hormuz is open and mines have been cleared. Currently, no negotiations with Tehran are ongoing or planned.

Ali Rasoulnejad, a resident of Mahabad, was arrested by the Intelligence Force of the IRGC. He was detained yesterday and transferred to an unknown location. No further details about his situation have been released.

Abbas Araghchi stated that the Islamic Republic is sincerely implementing its commitments under the ceasefire agreement, but the US has disrupted the process by violating the agreement. He also said that the situation in the Strait of Hormuz cannot return to its state before March 2026 without considering the damages to Iran. These remarks were made during a meeting with his Qatari counterpart.
The VIP cafe in Tehran was closed by relevant authorities due to mandatory hijab issues. This action was reported by Harana News Agency. More details are provided in the continuation of the report.

The 40th-day memorial ceremony for Aref Khoshkar was held in Behesht Zahra, Tehran, attended by his family and citizens. Aref Khoshkar was one of the detainees of the 2022 nationwide protests. He was executed in July of this year in Qezel Hesar prison in Karaj.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated at the 21st Rajai Festival that our country is a victim of terror. He said either people are turned against each other or direct attacks occur. Pezeshkian added that the mistake is distancing from the people.

The Intelligence Organization of the IRGC warned about increasing social dissatisfaction and the possibility of street protests. It claimed that the opponents of the Islamic Republic have changed their strategy to activating internal crises and psychological warfare. It also alleged the identification of a secret Mossad structure operating inside Iran.

Donald Trump signed an executive order to change the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America. This decision was made following trade tensions between the US and Canada. Canadian officials have stated they will not recognize this name change.

Hassan Bandani, a 21-year-old auto body worker from Shahin Shahr, Isfahan, was arrested on July 19 after going to the Execution of Sentences Office at Dastgerd Prison in Isfahan and was transferred to solitary confinement. He was detained due to his participation in the December protests and causing disorder. Bandani remains in solitary confinement without access to a lawyer or phone.

The Trump administration has stated it does not wish to return to the terms of the initial June agreement with the Islamic Republic. This stance has hindered efforts by Qatar, Oman, and Pakistan to revive negotiations between Washington and Tehran. The White House has announced that no negotiations with the Islamic Republic are underway and that the naval blockade and economic exclusion operations will continue.

Mohsen Rezaei stated that if the blockade continues, the economic interests of the United States will be targeted 100%. He said that if fighting resumes, future wars will be different. Rezaei also announced the breaking of the naval blockade and the return of oil sales to pre-sanction levels.

Mohsen Rezaee, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, threatened Benjamin Netanyahu with death and said Netanyahu's mistakes have brought the end of Israel's existence closer. Rezaee denied the claim that the Islamic Republic planned to kill Donald Trump and his son, calling it a big lie. He also stated that if the Islamic Republic decides to take action, nothing will prevent it.

Ahmad Donyamali stated that he is trying to create an opportunity for Chadormalu to represent Iran in the next season of the AFC Champions League. He mentioned that this issue is one of the reasons for his impeachment and emphasized not to accuse the Minister of Sports of corruption. Previously, the impeachment reasons included administrative corruption and poor international performance.

Thomas Juneau stated that the Strait of Hormuz remains a major concern for the US and that the Islamic Republic can endure economic pressures in the short and medium term. He added that both sides are currently unwilling to resume direct war, but the situation is fragile. Despite damage to its military capabilities, the Islamic Republic still retains the ability to target the Strait of Hormuz and regional infrastructure.

Mohsen Namjoo returned to Iran after about 29 years living abroad. He stated that he might resume his artistic activities and stage performances. The Minister of Culture also mentioned reviewing the possibility of the return of over 100 Iranian figures living abroad.
The White House has stated that no negotiations are underway. The deadlock between Tehran and Washington continues. This topic was discussed in the audio version of 24 with Fardad Farahzad.

Ebrahim Azizi, head of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, told the US government on X that the only remaining way is to surrender and accept all Tehran's conditions. He emphasized that any talks must be conducted from a position of strength and with acceptance of the realities on the ground. These statements were made on Thursday.

Reports indicate that crude oil flow from the Strait of Hormuz has gradually increased, with Middle Eastern producers except Iran raising their exports. Donald Trump stated that 24 tankers passed through the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday evening. This increase has helped contain prices, but transit through the strait remains risky.

The US State Department's "Rewards for Justice" program announced that it is still seeking information about Mohammad Bagher Shirinkar and Fatemeh Sedighian Kashi, two Iranian hackers linked to the "Shahid Shoushtari" group affiliated with the IRGC's Cyber-Electronic Command. The US had previously offered a reward of up to $10 million for information leading to the identification and location of these two individuals.

Barcelona defeated Athletic Bilbao 2-0 in the postponed first week match of La Liga. The goals were scored by Rafinha and Fermin Lopez. With this win, Barcelona moved to the top of the La Liga standings.

The Wall Street Journal reported that the Trump administration has repeatedly stated it is not interested in returning to the Islamabad agreement, complicating diplomatic efforts. Since the agreement ended, Trump has focused on economic pressure against the Islamic Republic. Mediators' efforts to reduce Iran's demands and resume negotiations have made little progress.

The Washington Times wrote that US sanctions policy against Iran faces a major challenge because Iran is no longer dependent on the Western financial system. China and Russia have enabled Iran's continued economic activity by creating alternative payment systems and channels. The newspaper emphasized that the US should target Chinese financial institutions and networks linked to Russia.

Donald Trump emphasized that the passage of ships through the Strait of Hormuz does not mean the end of US military actions. These remarks were made amid the continuation of the naval blockade of the Islamic Republic and the intensification of Washington's economic pressure on Tehran.

Meysam Mehrani said economic pressures have shifted the balance in favor of the US and placed the Islamic Republic in a difficult position. He pointed to long gasoline lines and the economic crisis as signs of government problems. Mehrani added that the Trump administration aims to maintain economic pressure to gain the upper hand in potential negotiations.

Al Jazeera reported that there is hope for reaching an agreement in Tehran and a space for negotiation and mediation has been formed. However, no agreement has been reached yet, and the Islamic Republic is currently in talks with mediators including Qatar and Pakistan. Talks between Iran and Oman and other Gulf countries are expected to continue.

Amirhossein Mirasmaeili said the disagreement between supporters of a deal with the US and the faction close to the IRGC has put the Islamic Republic in a risky position. He added that while some officials talk about negotiations, others increase the risk of war by threatening the US. Additionally, the economic crisis and protests have increased pressure on the Islamic Republic.

The White House spokesperson stated that currently there are no negotiations between Washington and Tehran. Trump has kept all options, including a naval blockade, on the table. The Basij commander said that every Iranian is ready to confront the enemy in the state of neither war nor peace.

Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting's Channel 3 has aired a video and spoken of setting a $10 million reward for the elimination of the youngest son of the US president. The US Secret Service has announced it is investigating the threat.

Alireza Nourizadeh said Qatar and Oman are trying to prevent the escalation of the crisis, but US economic pressures limit these efforts. The Trump administration believes that a compromise with the Islamic Republic will not be sustainable. Internal conflicts in the Islamic Republic have also intensified due to the absence of Mojtaba Khamenei.

Donald Trump criticized Fox News' report about the Islamic Republic as particularly false and claimed that Iranian officials want to negotiate with the US. He said he does not want to meet them, but they are begging for a deal. Trump also described Iran as a country in collapse.

The Turkish foreign minister welcomed the dissolution of the Syrian Democratic Forces and their integration into the Syrian army. He emphasized that Ankara will closely monitor the implementation of this decision. This report was provided by Narges Horkhsh from Iran International.

Nikki Haley accused China of financially supporting the Iranian government in its war against the US. She also stated that China hacks critical US infrastructure. These remarks coincided with the planned meeting between Trump and Xi Jinping.

Daily Sun reported that the war in Iran has reached a costly and dangerous stalemate after six months. The Islamic Republic faces sanctions and economic blockade but still holds power. Washington has shifted pressure to Iran's oil revenues and trade partners.

Bloomberg reported that Venezuela is considering plans to leave OPEC. The issue was also raised in the country's talks with US officials. No final decision has been made yet, and Reuters has not been able to independently confirm the report.

US intelligence agencies believe the Kremlin views the Iran war as weakening Washington's military capability. The CIA chief warned Russia about escalating the Ukraine war. The Trump administration denied ammunition shortages but called for increased production.

Haaretz wrote in an analysis that the sharp decline in Iran's oil exports could limit the financial resources of the IRGC and security agencies. The analysis suggests that reduced oil revenue may decrease the government's ability to suppress protests. However, the extent of alternative resources and the impact of economic pressure on the power structure remain unclear.

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, intends to urge G20 members to enforce sanctions on Iran's government at the financial meeting in Asheville, North Carolina. A US Treasury official said Bessent will work to expand Iran's economic isolation. China, as the largest buyer of Iranian oil, is one of the main challenges to this campaign.

Brad Cooper, CENTCOM commander, stated that US forces have protected the passage of nearly 1,500 ships carrying about 750 million barrels of crude oil through the Strait of Hormuz in recent months. The US has cleared mines planted by the IRGC, keeping international routes open. Washington continues the naval blockade of Iran, halting oil exports from Iranian ports.

New Zealand's Foreign Ministry stated it will not take a position at this stage regarding the US economic exclusion campaign against the Islamic Republic. The country supports UN Security Council sanctions as long as they comply with international law. New Zealand has also sanctioned some Iranian individuals and companies involved in supporting Russia's war in Ukraine.

Israeli forces entered the village of Briqueh in southern Syria and inspected several houses. The Israeli army announced it killed two Hamas members in Gaza. Additionally, Israeli artillery and air strikes were reported in areas of Lebanon.

The Israeli website Ynet wrote in an analysis that the Islamic Republic is facing complex crises including the collapse of the rial's value, economic pressures, and increasing internal dissatisfaction. The media predicted that this situation could lead to a new round of protests. It also mentioned that the intensification of mandatory hijab and failure to avenge Ali Khamenei are factors increasing dissatisfaction.

Erfan Ghanei-Fard stated that David Barnea's view on continuing pressure on the Islamic Republic until the regime falls overlaps with Israel's approach. This strategy includes economic pressure, security operations, and internal protests. He added that Israel's policy towards the Islamic Republic is not dependent on Netanyahu, and security agencies act independently.

Esmail Hajizadeh stated that 20,000 workers in Hormozgan province have become unemployed due to recession and business closures. The five-star Persian Gulf Hotel in Bandar Abbas and several other companies have laid off their staff. Many unemployed workers have turned to informal jobs, and workers' purchasing power has significantly decreased.

Agents of the Islamic Republic raided the homes and workplaces of Baha'is in seven provinces within less than a week and confiscated their belongings. At least 11 people have been arrested, and cars, cash, jewelry, computers, work tools, and children's toys were seized. This information was announced in a statement received by Iran International.

Atena Hosseinian was killed on January 8th during protests in Gorgan in front of the city governor's office. She was shot directly in the head by government forces. This incident occurred in the presence of her family members.

New Zealand's Foreign Ministry told Iran International that it is reviewing the new US 'economic exclusion' campaign against the Islamic Republic but is not commenting at this time. The New Zealand government emphasized its support for Security Council sanctions and described its trade volume with Iran as very limited. Australia's Foreign Ministry did not state a position on joining the new sanctions.

Two Caspian seals' carcasses were found on the Babolsar coast. With this, the number of casualties of this species in Mazandaran has reached 27. The exact cause of death could not be determined due to the advanced decomposition of the carcasses.
Harald V, the King of Norway, passed away at the age of 89. He was hospitalized last week due to a rare blood disease. His son Haakon will succeed him.

The football teams Foolad Khuzestan and Esteghlal will face each other today in the fourth week of the Premier League in Ahvaz. The match will take place this afternoon. To participate in the poll, visit the Iran International Sports Instagram page.

Amir Giti from Iran International said Donald Trump believes Iranian officials are begging to negotiate with the US. He added that Trump no longer seems willing to negotiate, while Iran is still seeking dialogue. Also, Iran considered the Strait of Hormuz a trump card, but this leverage ultimately benefited the US.
On Thursday night, a deep lunar eclipse was visible in parts of the world. This astronomical event was one of the most spectacular. A similar event will not occur again for another 18 years.

A citizen criticized rising prices in a video sent to Iran International, stating that the wages for three days of work only cover one day of food for the family. He pointed to the high costs. This highlights the economic pressure on families.

A video from Iran International shows that following the nationwide gasoline crisis in Iran, a long gasoline queue formed in the Kianmehr neighborhood of Ahvaz. This queue formed overnight on Thursday evening.

Hossein Alizadeh stated that Donald Trump has less inclination to negotiate with the Islamic Republic and that the US has changed its tactic to economic pressure and isolation. The goal is to force the Islamic Republic to change its behavior. Trump believes that increased economic pressure and internal problems could push the government to retreat and make concessions.

The Eritrean government announced that the oil tanker Sibo One, despite flying the Eritrean flag, is not registered in the country. The tanker was hijacked last week off the coast of Yemen by suspected pirates and diverted towards Somalia. Reports indicate that the Houthis have provided Somali pirates with GPS devices to help them track commercial ships more accurately.

The meeting of three European and four regional countries about the Strait of Hormuz, scheduled for August 30 in Istanbul, has been postponed. Foreign ministers of Germany, Britain, Pakistan, Turkey, France, Egypt, and Saudi Arabia were expected to attend. Egypt's foreign minister requested the postponement due to scheduling conflicts, and no new date has been set.

The Iranian national basketball team lost 93-91 to New Zealand in the first match of the second round of the 2027 World Cup qualifiers. Iran performed well in the fourth quarter but was defeated in overtime. Iran's next game will be against the Philippines on Sunday, August 30.

Recently, 11 Bahá'í citizens in seven provinces of Iran have been arrested or sent to prison. Their personal belongings and livelihood equipment have been confiscated by authorities. The Bahá'í International Community has expressed concern about these actions and the economic pressure on families.

A citizen in a video to Iran International says that fuel shortages are rampant in various cities, especially in this city. The fuel crisis in these areas has been reported as severe. This issue has caused concerns.

Rouhollah Rahimpour stated that Qatar and Pakistan are mediating between the Islamic Republic and the US. The main focus is on the Strait of Hormuz and restoring normal ship traffic. The goal is not to resolve disputes between Tehran and Washington.

The detention order for Soraya Manouchehrzadeh, Shima Sanaei, and Fakhereh Zahedi has been extended for one month. These three Baha'i citizens have been detained for seven days and are held in Tircola prison in Sari. They have been denied access to a lawyer and contact with their families.
Esmaeil Kowsari, a member of parliament, stated that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has had plans to close the Strait of Hormuz since 1987.

Messages received by Iran International indicate that economic pressure has forced many families to eliminate travel, cultural goods, and some non-food items. Workers have also reported non-payment of unemployment insurance and related livelihood problems. More details were provided by Leila Saadati.

Times of Israel reported that the US president is unwilling to revive the interim agreement with the Islamic Republic and prefers a maximum economic pressure strategy. According to the report, the Iranian government repeatedly violated the agreement at the last moments. Therefore, Donald Trump no longer accepts the terms of the previous memorandum.

A citizen reported in a video that they paid nearly 800,000 tomans for a few grocery items. They protested against those responsible for the price increases. This report was published by Iran International.

Ali Shirazi referred to the report by the Iran Human Rights organization about the increase in executions. He said the Islamic Republic uses executions to create fear and terror. The reason for this action is the fear of renewed protests in Iran.

The Wall Street Journal reported that Bank Melli Iran continues to operate in Dubai despite US demands to close its branches. The US Treasury Secretary has called for all branches of Bank Melli Iran to be shut down. The bank also has branches in several European countries that remain active.

Ahmad Donyamali, the Minister of Sports and Youth, commented on financial violations in the Taekwondo Federation and expressed hope that this issue would not affect the national team's preparation. He stated that oversight bodies have the right to intervene, but no specific information is yet available. The minister emphasized the need to support colleagues until final rulings are issued.

The planned meeting on the situation of the Strait of Hormuz in Istanbul has been canceled. The meeting was initiated by Germany and Turkey and canceled at Egypt's request. No new date has been announced for the meeting.

Hossein Aghaei said the Islamic Republic is losing one of its most important levers. Ship traffic in the Strait of Hormuz has not returned to pre-war conditions. US economic pressure could further weaken Tehran's position.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh responded to Mohammad Jafar Ghaempanah's remarks about enrichment and the US. He said these statements contradict the nature of the Islamic Republic and the philosophy of resistance. Ghazizadeh warned that continuing this duality could lead to structural cracks and ultimately the collapse of the regime.

The second hearing of Vahid Abiri's case was held at the Old Bailey court in London. He was arrested by counter-terrorism police and accused of cooperating with a foreign intelligence service. This report was provided by Ali Rashid from Iran International.

A video has emerged showing a citizen protesting against the IRGC and Basij during nighttime government gatherings. The person refers to them as symbols of oppression. This video has been shared publicly.

Soheila Hejab, detained during the December 2025 protests, has been held in uncertain conditions in Karaj's Kachouyi prison for nearly eight months. She remains in custody, and a bail of four billion tomans has been set for her temporary release. This information was reported by the HRANA news agency.

Water has been cut off in Safadasht from midnight on Thursday, September 5, until 2 PM on Friday, September 6. Internet in Tabriz has become very weak and VPNs are not working. Snapp drivers complain about the possible internet shutdown and economic difficulties.

Mohammad Javad Haj Ali Akbari stated that supporting the family and promoting a chaste lifestyle is a duty of the government. He criticized the anti-hijab policies during the Pahlavi era and called the promotion of immorality a factor weakening the family. He also urged media and elites to work towards protecting the family.

Saeed Fattahi, the football organization manager of Esteghlal club, expressed hope that FIFA will allow the club to sign three free agents. He mentioned that the Iranian transfer window is closed but lawyers have suggested sending a letter to FIFA. Fattahi also emphasized that Yaser Asani has no issue playing for Esteghlal, while Mes Shahr-e Babak club has filed an official complaint to the disciplinary committee.

The Ministry of Intelligence of the Islamic Republic of Iran announced the arrest of 30 citizens in the Mahalat and Nimvar counties of Markazi province. These individuals were arrested due to their participation in the protests of Dey 1404. The announcement was made by the Ministry of Intelligence.

The Human Rights Organization for Sports reported the death sentence for five athletes arrested during the "Iranian National Revolution." These individuals have been denied access to a lawyer of their choice. They are on the verge of execution.

Hassan Alidadi-Soleimani, the Friday prayer leader of Kerman, stated that the Islamic Republic will not retreat from its nuclear rights and sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz. He also said that the position of the Islamic Republic in the region has become clearer as America's allies weaken.

Yayoi Kusama, the avant-garde Japanese artist, passed away at the age of 97. She was one of the influential figures in contemporary art. News of her death was widely covered in major newspapers in Japan and worldwide.

A Revolutionary Guards commander with experience suppressing opponents of Bashar al-Assad in Syria was in charge of suppressing protests in Shahriar. Proxy forces were also present in some counties of Tehran province. Farzad Fattahi has provided explanations about these suppressions.

On September 6th, a video from Tehran showed a long line of cars at the Yadegar Imam highway area waiting for gasoline. The video was sent by a viewer of Iran International. The issue of gasoline queues in Tehran has attracted attention.

Reza Zangeneh, a 27-year-old from Malayer, has been sentenced to death by the Revolutionary Court of Karaj on charges of collaborating with Mossad and waging war. His case has been sent to the Supreme Court with a 12-day deadline for appeal. Before his arrest, Zangeneh worked as a foreign car mechanic and had recently married.

Reza Nouri, the Friday prayer leader of Bojnord, said that economic pressure on the US is severe and Trump's popularity has dropped below 30%. He added that the war with the US is no longer existential and that US military reserves have diminished. He also emphasized that the Strait of Hormuz is a strong point Iran maintains to exert economic pressure on the US.

Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, Qatar's Prime Minister, met with Masoud Pezeshkian, Iran's head of government, in Tehran on Thursday. The meeting took place as Qatar seeks to revive stalled diplomacy six months after the war began. Al Thani emphasized the importance of maintaining freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz according to international law.

The German Foreign Ministry condemned Abolfazl Shekarchi's threats against Persian-speaking journalists abroad. The German government rejects any threats and restrictions on press freedom. This response came after the recent threats by the senior spokesperson of the Islamic Republic's armed forces.

Bayern Munich has started the new Bundesliga season aiming to win the treble. The team won the first trophy of the season by defeating Dortmund in the German Supercup. The club management is satisfied with the team's progress under Vincent Kompany's leadership.

An oil tanker carrying gasoline and diesel has docked at the export pier of Kharg Island after about 40 days. The tanker is there to supply fuel for the island's power turbine tanks. This news was reported by a viewer of Iran International.

On Thursday, 5 Shahrivar, victims of the online investment group FNDK gathered in Talesh. The protest was due to the non-return of investors' funds. The prosecutor of Talesh announced that the case is under judicial investigation.

A severe storm with winds over 140 km/h hit Paris and surrounding areas. Dozens of trees fell on roads and railway lines, injuring at least one person. Rescue teams conducted about 60 operations to address flooding and storm damage.

Jafar Qaderi, a member of the Parliament's Economic Commission, criticized the Central Bank's currency policies to control the dollar price and said the Central Bank has lost its way. He added that the Central Bank's purchase of currency increased demand and liquidity, contributing to higher exchange rates and inflation. Qaderi believes the Central Bank may be trying to reduce liquidity and lower the currency price.
